questions.q: How should you treat the example figures in this capstone, such as $5.2M closed won and 27% win rate?
options: As real Cobalt Ridge data you must reproduce exactly in any org
As Salesforce-mandated benchmarks
As illustrative examples; your own org's numbers will differ and the method is what matters
As upper limits your dashboard must not exceed
questions.explain: Cobalt Ridge is fictional and the numbers are illustrative so all six lessons stay consistent. Your org will show different values.

questions.q: With a $8.0M target and $5.2M closed won, what is the remaining gap?
questions.explain: $8.0M minus $5.2M leaves $2.8M. Pipeline coverage is measured against this remaining gap, not against the full target.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of the capstone's four build stages?
options: Secure it, connect Data Cloud, model the metric layer, build the app
Build the app, model the metric layer, connect Data Cloud, secure it
Model the metric layer, secure it, build the app, connect Data Cloud
Connect Data Cloud, build the app, secure it, model the metric layer
questions.explain: You build the app first, define the metrics centrally, add Data Cloud usage data, then secure the whole thing before presenting.

questions.q: Why does this course note that Data Cloud was rebranded Data 360?
options: Because the feature was removed and replaced by CRM Analytics
Because the two are separate products with different licenses
Because Salesforce renames products often, so learners should verify names and menus for their release
Because only Data 360 supports calculated insights
questions.explain: Names, menus, and features change between releases. The capability is the same; check current documentation for the label your org shows.

questions.q: In the example baseline, 17 renewal accounts fall under 40% seat activation and hold $2.3M of ARR, out of $12.4M renewing in 90 days. Roughly what share of renewing ARR is at risk?
options: About 8%
About 12%
About 27%
About 19%
questions.explain: $2.3M divided by $12.4M is about 18.5%, so roughly 19% of the renewing ARR shows weak adoption.
